newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, AGAs seen neutral.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, AGAs seen neutral.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas, helped by firmer physical prices and technical buying, ended higher Wednesday in a fairly active session, then reacted little to a neutral weekly AGA stock report, sources said.

May climbed 6.8 cents to close at $2.005 per million British thermal units, then held steady on ACCESS after the inventory data. June settled 7.1 cents higher at $2.046. Other deferreds ended up by 0.3 to 5.7 cents.
"The AGAs were within expectations. I don't think they will squelch the rally, but if we get May up to $2.05, I'd be looking for a place to sell it," said a Texas-based trader.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 16 bcf, in line with expectations. Overall stocks are still 290 bcf, or 53 percent, above year-ago, with eastern inventories, which fell last week by 23 bcf, still more than double 1996's record lows.

Chart traders said May's close today above $2, a four-week high, was technically constructive and would likely lead to more upside. They pegged next resistance at $2.05 and $2.095. Support points were seen at $1.925, $1.88, $1.85 and $1.825.
June, which broke a double top at $2.03 and hit a four-week high of $2.05, also looked bullish, they said.
Temperatures through most of the East and upper Midwest were expected to remain below-normal through the week.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices were steady to up slightly Wednesday at about the $2 level. Midcontinent pipes were little changed in the mid-$1.80s. Gas at the New York city gate was quoted up slightly to the mid-to-high $2.30s.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip jumped 4.7 cents to $2.184. NYMEX said 46,206 Hub contracts traded, up from Tuesday's revised tally of 30,124.
No NYMEX Permian or Alberta gas contracts traded Wednesday.

On the KCBT, May finished eight cents higher at $1.89, while deferreds ended up by two to 6.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.2 cents to 11.5 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 314 lots changed hands, up from Tuesday's total of 179.
